title: Kirkeby leaves the band behind for Fats's Europe trip and 'Stormy Weather'
summary: Kirkeby talked Fats out of taking the six-piece band to Europe and to Hollywood, using hired substitutes to save money.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Herman, what was Fats's attitude about what was happening to Rudy, about Rudy not getting any --
Well Fats says well, I've got to -- whatever's right to be done, do it. I -- that's the end. He would take off.

Everybody, yeah, to Kirkaby, yeah, take care of this, like the first time he went to Europe. We were supposed to have gone with him, the band, the six pieces, and he talked -- Kirkaby talked Fats out of it. And we were standing at the boat, at that time we go on the -- what? -- Queen Mary, one of those big boats. And we were standing down there like little fools, to the last minute. Well we -- he said Kirkaby's here. He'll be here. He'll tell you what to do.
We were packed and waiting, and hoping, and the last minute -- we didn't see Kirkaby. Fats said well, fellows, bye, I'll see you when I come back. You know.
You mean nobody told you in advance that you'd be --
Naw, right to the last minute Kirkaby told Fats that -- ah, it was too expensive, and he could save

money by not taking the band, and he could hire some musicians after he got over there, and do this, and save, and he did the same thing when they made "Stormy Weather". We were supposed to have gone out there to do that with him. Kirkoby talked him into hiring some standbys, and so and so and so and so on, so I can put the other money in my pocket, and that's just what he did.
Is that why, on the records in Europe, there was different -- a whole different band?
And the records in California was a whole different band?
That's right, a whole different thing. That's right.
